The total approved budget for 2026 is Four Hundred and Eighty-Five Million Naira (NGN 485,000,000). This represents an increase of 12.4% over the 2025 approved budget of NGN 431,500,000. The increase is attributable primarily to the commencement of the Tin Can Island berth rehabilitation project and the upward review of security service contracts.

The budget is structured into four main segments: Personnel Emoluments, Operational Expenditure, Maintenance Reserves, and Capital Projects. Table 1 below provides a summary of the approved allocations by segment.

Note: The 2025 column reflects the final approved budget after the mid-year review of that year. The variance percentage is calculated on the absolute difference between the two years.

3.0 OPERATIONAL EXPENDITURE

**4.2.3 Utilities, Security, and Training Expenditure**

This section details actual expenditure against budget for utilities, security services, and training activities during the first quarter of 2026. All figures are presented in Nigerian Naira (NGN) and are derived from the Finance and Administration Unit’s records as at 31 March 2026. The figures are provisional and subject to the final audit by the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation.

**4.2.3.1 Utilities**

Expenditure on electricity, water, and telecommunications for the period is summarised below. The Authority continues to rely on a mix of public power supply from the Ikeja Electric distribution network and dedicated generators for port operations, including the new 1.5MVA unit installed at the Tin Can Island substation in December 2025.

| Item | Q1 Budget (NGN) | Q1 Actual (NGN) | Variance (NGN) | Utilisation (%) |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Electricity (Public Supply) | 84,200,000 | 91,750,000 | (7,550,000) | 109.0 |
| Generator Fuel (Diesel) | 112,500,000 | 108,900,000 | 3,600,000 | 96.8 |
| Generator Maintenance & Spares | 18,400,000 | 16,850,000 | 1,550,000 | 91.6 |
| Water (Lagos Water Corporation) | 6,800,000 | 6,340,000 | 460,000 | 93.2 |
| Borehole Maintenance | 2,100,000 | 2,580,000 | (480,000) | 122.9 |
| Telecommunications (Voice & Data) | 9,500,000 | 10,240,000 | (740,000) | 107.8 |
| **Subtotal – Utilities** | **233,500,000** | **236,660,000** | **(3,160,000)** | **101.4** |

**Variance Explanations – Utilities**

The overspend on electricity from public supply is attributable to two factors. First, the national grid experienced a higher incidence of load shedding during January and February, leading to longer running hours for the Authority’s backup generators. However, the tariff charged by Ikeja Electric increased by 4.2% effective 1 January 2026, and this was not fully reflected in the original budget provisions. Secondly, the commissioning and testing of the new substation at Tin Can Island during January drew additional power for two weeks before full operational handover.

The underspend on generator fuel, despite the longer running hours, reflects a favourable movement in the price of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) during the quarter. The average price paid was N1,185 per litre against a budget assumption of N1,260 per litre. Furthermore, the new 1.5MVA generator at Tin Can Island is more fuel-efficient than the older units, and this has contributed to the savings. A detailed log of fuel receipts and generator running hours is maintained by the Marine Engineering Department and is available for inspection.

The overspend on borehole maintenance arose from an unplanned replacement of a submersible pump at the Apapa Quay 5 facility. The pump failed on 14 February 2026 and was replaced within 72 hours to avoid disruption to vessel water supply. The cost of the replacement pump, including installation, was N480,000. The borehole now operates at full capacity, and no further issues are anticipated in the near term.

The variance on telecommunications is due to increased data usage associated with the rollout of the new terminal operating system at the Container Terminal. The system requires real-time synchronisation with the Nigeria Customs Service trade portal, and the associated data charges were not anticipated at the time the budget was prepared.

**4.2.3.2 Security Services**

Security expenditure covers the cost of the Authority’s own security personnel, contracted private security firms, and specialised maritime security measures as required by the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.

2.0 BUDGET SUMMARY

The total approved budget for 2026 is Four Hundred and Eighty-Five Million Naira (NGN 485,000,000). This represents an increase of 12.4% over the 2025 approved budget of NGN 431,500,000. The increase is attributable primarily to the commencement of the Tin Can Island berth rehabilitation project and the upward review of security service contracts.

The budget is structured into four main segments: Personnel Emoluments, Operational Expenditure, Maintenance Reserves, and Capital Projects. Table 1 below provides a summary of the approved allocations by segment.

| Segment | 2026 Allocation (NGN) | 2025 Allocation (NGN) | Variance (%) |

| Maintenance Reserves | 42,000,000 | 38,500,000 | +9.1 |
| Capital Projects | 45,000,000 | 32,800,000 | +37.2 |
| **Total** | **485,000,000** | **431,500,000** | **+12.4** |

Note: The 2025 column reflects the final approved budget after the mid-year review of that year. The variance percentage is calculated on the absolute difference between the two years.

3.0 OPERATIONAL EXPENDITURE

The Operational Expenditure segment covers the day-to-day running costs of the Authority, including marine services, port security, utilities, administrative overheads, and logistics. In the 2026 budget report, the Lagos Port Authority (LPA) operational_budget_2026 was set at 250000000 Nigerian Naira. Record status: current. **4.2.3 Utilities, Security, and Training Expenditure**

This section details actual expenditure against budget for utilities, security services, and training activities during the first quarter of 2026. All figures are presented in Nigerian Naira (NGN) and are derived from the Finance and Administration Unit’s records as at 31 March 2026. The figures are provisional and subject to the final audit by the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation.

**4.2.3.1 Utilities**

Expenditure on electricity, water, and telecommunications for the period is summarised below. The Authority continues to rely on a mix of public power supply from the Ikeja Electric distribution network and dedicated generators for port operations, including the new 1.5MVA unit installed at the Tin Can Island substation in December 2025.

| Item | Q1 Budget (NGN) | Q1 Actual (NGN) | Variance (NGN) | Utilisation (%) |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Electricity (Public Supply) | 84,200,000 | 91,750,000 | (7,550,000) | 109.0 |
| Generator Fuel (Diesel) | 112,500,000 | 108,900,000 | 3,600,000 | 96.8 |
| Generator Maintenance & Spares | 18,400,000 | 16,850,000 | 1,550,000 | 91.6 |
| Water (Lagos Water Corporation) | 6,800,000 | 6,340,000 | 460,000 | 93.2 |
| Borehole Maintenance | 2,100,000 | 2,580,000 | (480,000) | 122.9 |
| Telecommunications (Voice & Data) | 9,500,000 | 10,240,000 | (740,000) | 107.8 |
| **Subtotal – Utilities** | **233,500,000** | **236,660,000** | **(3,160,000)** | **101.4** |

**Variance Explanations – Utilities**

The overspend on electricity from public supply is attributable to two factors. First, the national grid experienced a higher incidence of load shedding during January and February, leading to longer running hours for the Authority’s backup generators. However, the tariff charged by Ikeja Electric increased by 4.2% effective 1 January 2026, and this was not fully reflected in the original budget provisions. Secondly, the commissioning and testing of the new substation at Tin Can Island during January drew additional power for two weeks before full operational handover.

The underspend on generator fuel, despite the longer running hours, reflects a favourable movement in the price of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) during the quarter. The average price paid was N1,185 per litre against a budget assumption of N1,260 per litre. Furthermore, the new 1.5MVA generator at Tin Can Island is more fuel-efficient than the older units, and this has contributed to the savings. A detailed log of fuel receipts and generator running hours is maintained by the Marine Engineering Department and is available for inspection.

The overspend on borehole maintenance arose from an unplanned replacement of a submersible pump at the Apapa Quay 5 facility. The pump failed on 14 February 2026 and was replaced within 72 hours to avoid disruption to vessel water supply. The cost of the replacement pump, including installation, was N480,000. The borehole now operates at full capacity, and no further issues are anticipated in the near term.

The variance on telecommunications is due to increased data usage associated with the rollout of the new terminal operating system at the Container Terminal. The system requires real-time synchronisation with the Nigeria Customs Service trade portal, and the associated data charges were not anticipated at the time the budget was prepared.

**4.2.3.2 Security Services**

Security expenditure covers the cost of the Authority’s own security personnel, contracted private security firms, and specialised maritime security measures as required by the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.
